Our competitive code, constructed preferences and fitted additions are
Copyright (c) 2026 zkasuran, LicenseRef-zkasuran-SAND-1.0. These terms apply
only to our own portions and do not restrict retained upstream grants.

Source experiment revision 2 retains the complete original SAND grant in
SAND-1.0.txt and clarifies source/checkpoint scope in LICENSE. Training and
validation source rows remain unchanged. The scored original audit from run
44682766454 is excluded from all new fitting and evaluation. Fresh audit groups
include licensed publications through 2026 with separate source/entity identities.
The new audit is not scored until the frozen candidate passes development gates.

Training-only diagnostic mode compares source-role binding and a single requested
reference on four existing training groups. It records real gradients, parameter
changes and train-fit metrics, not held-out quality or registration readiness.
The fresh audit remains unscored after the second development failure.

Revision 3 uses a train-only requested-reference warm-up over all original
training rows before the original two-reference main task. The title associations
and complete source abstracts keep their CC BY 4.0 grants and original attribution.
The constructed training view and fitted additions use the unchanged reviewed
SAND grant. Neither the warm-up nor the tiny training diagnostic is an audit.

Matched batching diagnostics retain original complete two-reference prompts and
published titles on four existing training groups. No new preference labels or
held-out data are introduced. Metrics are fitted training controls, not audited
capability. Warm-up checkpoints now receive the same full grant sidecars as main
checkpoints; previously stamped tensor bytes remain covered by retained grants.

Revision 4 role bootstrap repeats eight unchanged original training pairs from
four existing source groups before full main training. Repetitions are disclosed
and do not count as new source groups or annotations. Original per-article grants
and attribution are retained. Our training schedule and fitted additions use
SAND only on our own portions, including incomplete or failed checkpoints.
